issue: Threatened to contact someone or share information improperly

themes.label: Debt disclosed to family members
themes.description: Consumers allege collectors contacted or shared debt details with parents, children, spouses, siblings, or other relatives by phone, text, email, or served documents.

examples.summary: Consumer claims debt collector contacted their mother and other relatives via text messages about their debt.

A debt collection agency sent a collection text message to the consumer's mother's phone number using an unverified skip-traced contact, disclosing the consumer's debt account information to an unauthorized third party.
A debt collection company allegedly made repeated calls to the consumer and the consumer's father requesting personal information without providing prior written documentation of a debt.

themes.label: Employer or coworker contacted about debt
themes.description: Consumers allege collectors contacted employers, supervisors, or workplaces, or contacted other third parties such as landlords and roommates, to locate the consumer or discuss the debt.

examples.summary: A debt collector allegedly contacted the consumer's employer and spouse to collect a debt, disclosed protected medical information without authorization, and had previously attempted to collect a debt the consumer claims was not owed.
Debt collector allegedly contacted consumer's son's employer to locate the debtor and disclosed the collection account details to the employer.

A collection agency allegedly contacted the consumer's employer, landlord, and mother to locate the consumer after the consumer requested they stop calling, despite the consumer claiming never to have used the company's service and not owing any debt.

themes.label: Contact continued despite stop or dispute requests
themes.description: Consumers allege collectors kept calling, emailing, or texting after cease-contact requests, disputes, or written-only communication demands.

examples.summary: Consumer claims a debt collector continued calling and leaving voicemails after sending a certified letter requesting information about a disputed debt.
Debt collector continued contacting consumer about an unrecognized account despite the consumer's disputes, requests for validation documentation, and requests to cease contact.

A debt collection firm sent written communication to a consumer who had previously filed a cease and desist order with the original creditor, allegedly violating the consumer's request to cease further communication.

themes.label: Inadequate validation, investigation, or inaccurate reporting
themes.description: Consumers allege collectors failed to validate or reasonably investigate disputed debts or reported inaccurate or conflicting account information.

examples.summary: Consumer claims that a debt collector is reporting multiple inaccurate accounts with Metro 2 compliance violations and failed to conduct a reasonable reinvestigation of disputed accounts despite formal disputes and validation requests.

Consumer claims a debt collection account is being reported inaccurately with misaligned balance, status, and payment history, and that a prior FCRA dispute was not reasonably investigated by the furnisher.

Consumer disputed a debt and requested validation pursuant to federal law, alleging the collector's response consisting only of a billing statement does not constitute proper verification of the debt's validity or the collector's legal right to collect.

themes.label: Unclear debt documentation and handling
themes.description: Consumers allege confusion or a lack of documentation, notice, or responsiveness about debt transfers, garnishment, or negotiation.

examples.summary: Consumer receiving collection letters from eight different companies regarding the same debt and alleges personal information and account details are being shared or transferred between companies without knowledge or explanation.
Consumer claims wages were garnished without prior written notice, explanation of the debt, or identification of the garnishing entity or timeline

Consumer claims a debt collector disconnected a call without documenting her account details after she became frustrated when the agent was not listening, following a 5-month communication gap with the collection agency regarding a disputed medical debt.

brief.headline: Third-party debt disclosure claims are steady, with little acceleration
brief.what_is_happening: Complaints about collectors allegedly threatening to contact or improperly share debt information with others are running slightly above baseline, not surging. The recent monthly average is 224.33 against a baseline of 211.17 (velocity 1.0609, rank 18 of 79). In an AI-reviewed sample of 40 narratives, the most common claims are that debt details were shared with family members (41.7%) and that employers or coworkers were contacted (22.2%). Other claims include contact continuing after stop or dispute requests (11.1%) and inadequate validation or inaccurate reporting (13.9%). These are unverified allegations.
brief.who_is_affected: Consumers contacted by debt collectors, including debt buyers, collection agencies and credit reporting firms. Their relatives, employers and other third parties are also named in the narratives. Complaints are spread across states, led by FL (10.3%), TX (9.6%) and CA (9.3%). The AI sample put the vulnerable-consumer share at 7.5% and mean severity at 3.2 of 5.
brief.likely_root_cause: Hypothesis to test: third-party contact is happening during skip-tracing or location efforts, where weak contact-data verification, unclear limits on what may be said to non-debtors, and poor handling of cease-contact and dispute flags may let contact reach relatives or workplaces. Sample summaries mention unverified skip-traced numbers, texts to relatives, and contact after stop requests. The sample is small, so this needs testing against internal data.
brief.process_or_control_to_check: Check third-party contact and skip-trace procedures: how phone numbers and emails are validated before use, scripting and monitoring for location-only calls, suppression of contact after cease-contact or dispute requests, and controls on text, email and mailed-document channels. Also review dispute and validation handling, and QA call sampling for third-party disclosures.
brief.regulatory_area: Debt collection conduct, specifically third-party communications and disclosure of debt information, plus handling of disputes and validation requests
evidence: Recent monthly average of 224.33 complaints versus a baseline average of 211.17, a velocity of 1.0609 (rank 18 of 79).
Monthly counts ranged from 180 (2026-05) to 275 (2026-01) over the past 12 months, with 249 in 2026-07 and 218 in 2026-08.
Harris & Harris, Ltd. has the highest lift among top companies at 2.168 on 10 complaints; TRANSWORLD SYSTEMS INC has 1.476 on 13 complaints; EQUIFAX, INC. has 1.33 on 17 complaints.

Largest raw-count companies sit near or below proportional representation: ENCORE CAPITAL GROUP INC. 0.996 lift on 44 complaints, Resurgent Capital Services L.P. 1.107 on 41, CL Holdings LLC 0.549 on 33, Portfolio Recovery Associates, LLC 0.576 on 25.
Only 1.85% of 108 recent narratives appear templated, which suggests mostly individually written accounts.
In the AI sample of 40, 41.7% of narratives allege debt disclosed to family members and 22.2% allege employer or coworker contact.
In the AI sample, 11.1% allege contact continued after stop or dispute requests and 13.9% allege inadequate validation or inaccurate reporting.
AI-assessed mean severity is 3.2 of 5 and 7.5% of the sample involves vulnerable consumers.

checks.name: size
checks.reason: The brief names no specific company, and the largest companies sit near proportional representation (ENCORE lift 0.996 on 44 complaints, Resurgent 1.107 on 41), so this is a market-wide signal rather than a size artifact.

checks.name: templating
checks.reason: Only 1.85% of 108 recent narratives appear templated, well under the 30% threshold.

checks.name: concentration
checks.reason: The top state FL holds only 10.3% (TX 9.6%, CA 9.3%) and no company exceeds 44 complaints, so the signal is not confined to one state or one company.

checks.name: thin_evidence
checks.reason: The AI sample has 40 complaints and 108 recent narratives exist, and the third-party disclosure themes (family 41.7% plus employer 22.2%) cover about 64% of the sample, which supports the named third-party contact root cause.

checks.name: seasonality
checks.reason: The recent average of 224.33 rests on July's 249 (June 206, August 218), and without July the other two months average about 212, no higher than the 211.17 baseline, so the uplift comes from a single peak month.

skeptic.note: Rejected because the small 1.06 velocity is driven entirely by a single peak month (July 2026), so there is no sustained rise despite otherwise adequate evidence.
